whatChanged.title: Past language returned in real communication — and Gustavo began noticing his own answers
whatChanged.summary: Across the five lessons, Gustavo repeatedly used English to talk about his own world. Past language returned in different contexts instead of being treated as a one-off grammar topic. On 15 September, after answering a past question with “I don't”, he changed it to “No, I didn't”. He also reused went and drank in personal sentences. In Science, some language from the previous week was available again while other ideas needed another pass. This is evidence of movement, retrieval and noticing — not a claim that every form is already mastered independently.
whatChanged.evidence: Lessons 1–5: recurring past-language use in personal contexts; 15 Sep self-correction “I don't” → “No, I didn't”; reuse of went/drank; partial Science retrieval after one week.

priorities.title: Tell real stories about the past

priorities.title: Listen for NOW vs PAST

priorities.title: Try to retrieve before receiving help

priorities.title: Become a learning detective
priorities.why: Gustavo is beginning to notice his own language. Brief reflection can help him recognize what he used, what he corrected and what he wants to try again.
priorities.evidence: Lesson 5 self-correction provides a concrete starting point for learner self-awareness.

classReports.title: Class Report - 08 Sep 2026 — Science Intensive Review
classReports.summary: A 60-minute bilingual Science revision based on the school test notice. Gustavo worked through food and nutrients, vitamins and minerals, and the digestive system using visual review, guided recall, matching, gap-fill, reordering, sentence reconstruction and a final quiz.
classReports.teacherInsight: Primary transcript evidence shows successful supported retrieval. Gustavo repeated 'give us energy' for carbohydrates, classified foods, reconstructed the digestive route and correctly retrieved the large intestine as the site of water absorption. The lesson supports consolidation, not a claim of independent mastery of every item.

classReports.title: Class Report - 15 Sep 2026
classReports.summary: Returned to general English after the Science review. Gustavo checked Science memory after one week, contrasted Do/Did answers, reused past verbs and built personal sentences.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: After “Did you go...?”, Gustavo first answered “I don't” and then changed it to “No, I didn't”. He also reused went and drank in personal sentences and recalled part of the Science language after one week. Interpretation: Past meaning is returning across contexts and there is emerging evidence of self-monitoring while speaking. Boundary: One self-correction does not establish mastery, and Science recall varied between independent retrieval and reconstruction with support. Next verification: Invite a new real past story, contrast Do/Did, let Gustavo attempt retrieval before help, and use a short learner-awareness check-in.

grammarOverview.title: Language We Are Building
grammarOverview.summary: The aim is not to collect grammar labels. These language patterns matter because they help Gustavo tell stories, understand time, give advice, describe relationships between actions and people, compare things, and use English to learn.
focusPoints: Talking about past experiences: use forms such as went and drank, and didn't + base verb.
Understanding time in questions: Do...? usually asks about routines or the present; Did...? asks about completed past events.
Giving advice: use should / shouldn't to say what someone could do.
Actions that return to the same person: myself, yourself, himself, herself.
Comparing one thing with all the others: shorter words often use -est; longer words often use the most; some forms are irregular, such as best.
Science in English: useful academic vocabulary and sequencing remain available for reuse when relevant.

teacherFeedback.title: Your first five-lesson journey
teacherFeedback.body: Over these five lessons, Gustavo has been using English increasingly to talk about things that belong to his own world — holidays, school, sports, games and experiences. Talking about things that happened naturally brought past language into conversation. Those forms have returned several times: sometimes with a model or clue, sometimes through retrieval, and on 15 September through a clear self-correction. English was also used as a tool for Science. One week later, some of that language returned easily and some needed another pass. The important story is not simply what was right or wrong: it is that Gustavo is using, revisiting, noticing and reconnecting language over time.

teacherFeedback.title: Leitura pedagógica da jornada
teacherFeedback.body: Aprender não acontece em linha reta. Uma aula pode apresentar algo novo, fortalecer algo antigo, revelar um erro útil, recuperar uma ideia depois de alguns dias ou ajudar o aluno a perceber melhor o próprio inglês. O próximo ciclo vai preservar essa lógica: cada aula terá uma direção, sem exigir uma 'mudança de estado' artificial. Queremos que Gustavo se torne também um observador da própria aprendizagem — percebendo o que já consegue fazer, o que consegue tentar com ajuda e o que ainda quer estudar mais.

cumulativeImpact.title: Learning Journey — First 5 Lessons
cumulativeImpact.summary: Gustavo moved from reactivating English through personal conversation to repeatedly using past meaning in new contexts, preparing school content through English, retrieving part of that content after a week and beginning to notice and repair some of his own language. The journey is still in progress: repeated practice, support, reconstruction and consolidation are part of the movement, not evidence of failure.
evidence: 5/5 completed lessons confirmed: 18 Aug, 25 Aug, 01 Sep, 08 Sep and 15 Sep 2026.
Past meaning returned across personal conversation, school review and follow-up tasks rather than appearing only once.
15 Sep: self-correction from “I don't” to “No, I didn't” after a past question.
15 Sep: went and drank reused in personal sentences.
Science vocabulary and concepts showed mixed retrieval after one week: some remained available and some needed another pass.
No CEFR level change is claimed from these five lessons alone.
